name: Daman-e-Koh viewpoint
assumptions: Origin and suppress ring are the visitor core traced from satellite tiles, not the dossier's 412 m park outline, which runs up a steep hillside; lawns and the upper road are left to the game.
Deck heights: upper deck 3.3 m above the lower, read from the aerial photo; pavilion plaza 0.9 m above the upper deck; the dome platform 6 m above it is a visual estimate.
The real plaza and terrace levels are unsurveyed; roundabout and paths are placed at the lower-deck datum.
Rail height 1.1 m (dossier assumption); post spacing about 2.3 m and cable layout estimated from the 2008 deck photo; the photo's crossed cable infill is drawn one X to a bay.
Upper deck colour is the dossier value; lower deck is a dry pale pink-tan from the aerial photo and satellite, and the wet deck photo shows it much redder when wet.

Dome diameter 23 m, between the satellite's 21 by 27 m white patch and the aerial photo's ratio to the deck. Height over width 0.59 from the aerial photo: wall 4.6 m and shell 9 m are estimates. The photo shows about 4 windows on the visible half, so 10 evenly spaced windows are drawn; the unseen north side is assumed the same. The dark crown is a small closed cap from the satellite.
Two telescopes placed on the lower rim where one photo shows two pedestals; the real count is unknown and the head shape is generic.
Map board position inferred from a white upright in the aerial photo; the map face is a simplified colour diagram from a blurred photo of the board.

Pavilion outline from the satellite; posts, core and the ribbed Dutch-gable roof from one oblique aerial photo. Roof heights, rib spacing and lattice pattern are estimates, and the east gable is assumed to match the west one.

Annex, white block and masts north of the dome are read from one aerial photo. The photo crops the mast tops: 34 and 32 m are lower bounds scaled against the dome, so the masts end plainly with no invented top equipment. Lattice is drawn as a plain three-legged section. The manifest height is the occupied top, the dome crown; modelTop follows the masts in both LODs.
The separate mast cluster on the walled compound about 65 m north-west of the dome is outside the model and left out.

Hillside is one continuous estimated surface, joining the deck to the dome knoll as the aerial photo shows; no survey exists, so its slopes (about 0.55), the -16 m floor and the tree positions are invented to that general form. The game flattens the suppress ring at z 0, so only the parts above it show.

Roundabout radius from satellite, tiers and palm from one photo, palm height about 5 m and frond count estimated; six spiral lamps around it (four are visible), and lamp height 4.6 m estimated. Flower beds are drawn as a mass of low clumps; bloom colours vary by season. The plaza-side hedge beds are placed from two ground photos, their arcs are estimated.

Restaurant tables and umbrellas on the brick ring are movable and left out. Pots follow the dossier colours (red, white, purple); the three-row order red back, purple middle, white front comes from the review and could not be confirmed in the photos on disk.
Individual decked trees are limited to four standing on the decks; the forest is a mottled hill surface with low-poly crowns.
